summary: Suspicious patterns in solana-web3-community bundle require human review
details: The package ships large bundled files (lib/index.cjs.js and lib/index.esm.js) that contain co-occurring keywords commonly seen in both legitimate Web3/RPC libraries and exfiltration code: require('child_process'), fetch/POST/GET calls, and references to 'curl' and 'ping' strings. Without traced execution, it is not possible to determine from these matches alone whether the network calls are user-facing RPC client behavior (the documented purpose for a Solana web3 library, which legitimately performs HTTP POST/GET against RPC endpoints) or a hardcoded exfiltration channel. The package name also has surface similarity to the well-known @solana/web3.js library, which warrants reviewer attention to confusion risk. No specific attacker-controlled domain, install-time lifecycle hook, credential-path read, or wallet/seed-scanning fingerprint was identified in the provided evidence quotes. Routing to human review so a reviewer can de-minify the bundled files, confirm whether the fetch destinations are caller-supplied RPC URLs versus hardcoded endpoints, and assess name-confusion risk against @solana/web3.js.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
